description: We are a student team passionate about space exploration, physics, and scientific research. Our project focuses on developing a sustainable, self-sufficient network of human settlements on Mars. We aim to identify suitable locations and explore solutions for water, oxygen, food, energy, and resource utilization. We welcome curious and motivated teammates with interests in science, research, engineering, data analysis, mapping, and design.
summary: We looked into whether Mars could support life and came up with a plan for a robot to search for signs of life in places where there was water and under the ice. This helps create the science needed for people to live in areas of Mars.
details:
What it does: Mars Autonomous Civilization is a concept that is based on research for settling Mars as one system that has five regions (Arcadia Planitia, Elysium Planitia, Jezero Crater, Deuteronilus Mensae, Nili Fossae) of just one base. Robots. Build first then humans settle in only 2 to 3 core hubs while robots work in other places. The regions share resources and the need for help from Earth decreases slowly.

Benefits and impact: This approach reduces danger for people uses the strengths of each region and offers a research-based way to move from study to a Mars economy that can take care of itself.

Tools and data: We use data from NASA (RAD, InSight, Perseverance, MOXIE, radar and mineral research, MOLA, Mars Trek) and a 2025 JGR: Planets study. [Add any software that was used.]

Creativity: We think of Mars as a civilization with regions that have special roles and we always keep NASA-confirmed facts, research results and our own ideas separate.

Factors considered: Water and ice energy (including during winter) the shape of the land, minerals, scientific value, radiation, dust storms, cold, equipment breaking down delays, in communication and how safe it is to land.
